card.title: The One Who Lets You Win
card.instruction: Return to the familiar role of making victory easier for others, then let the cost of that generosity become impossible to ignore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my queen where you can take it. Same as last Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to beat you properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can. I've also stopped practising so you can catch up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come back to chess club with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. But introduce me as your old coach. They only know me as the person you keep beating.

mechanism: A resumes helping B win but exposes the lost competence and public identity that generosity costs.
confusable: Unlike mere martyrdom, A must first make victory easier and then reveal a concrete price of that recurring help.
comparison: S201-a seeks restored chess identity through B's invitation; S201-b seeks accurate credit while sheltering B's promotion.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
